correctness.rationale: For at most three stationary projective points, all equality/ternary-collinearity extension types are exhausted by 0/1/2 anchors, three collinear anchors, or three noncollinear anchors. The only field-order-dependent type is an additional point on a line already containing three distinct anchors, available iff q>=3. A noncollinear triangle has 3q points on its three sides and (q-1)^2>=1 points of the spanned projective plane off the sides; any ambient higher dimension contains that plane. The complete profile therefore supplies indefinite four-pebble replies for any same-category pair. Width-four separating formulas count at most four points and express noncollinearity. A width-five disjoint-line formula is false in every projective plane and true using two skew coordinate lines in dimension at least three. Finite checker verifies eight small prime-field spaces; the proof, not the finite sample, covers arbitrary dimensions and all fields.

originality.rationale: The available full-text comparisons concern general finite-variable pebble-game theory or two-sorted modal logics of projective planes. Neither derives the point-only ternary four-variable classification uniformly across projective dimensions. The closest accessible plane-only classifications concern structures of dimension two and do not entail the cross-dimensional equivalence. The 1998 finite-dimensional modal/Lyndon-algebra report is an identified access and priority uncertainty; its available description does not furnish the claimed four-variable first-order classification. Originality here is a best-knowledge claim, not a proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for all finite projective dimensions and field orders at a fixed logical width, rather than an arbitrary isolated computation. The result identifies an exact expressive-power boundary: dimension beyond a plane is invisible with four variables in point-collinearity logic but visible with five via skew lines. It also isolates only two nontrivial field-size classes among all ranks >=2 and gives a uniform proof valid even for non-Desarguesian finite projective planes. Unlike a small parameter improvement, the extra result is a global dimension-uniform logical collapse.
